title: PUC sues Paxton’s office over release of data center records
source_used: The Texas Tribune; text from WORKDIR/fulltext/C09-14.txt
key_facts: The Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUC) sued Attorney General Ken Paxton's office on Monday 5 Oct 2026 in Travis County.
It wants a judge to block release of two fields about data centers and crypto mines: county and regional water planning area, saying they could aid terrorists when combined with other survey data.
The PUC is not asking the court to make the whole survey confidential.
The attorney general's office issued two rulings that the PUC had not shown the information reveals vulnerabilities covered by the Homeland Security Act.
The 2025-mandated PUC survey went to 377 facilities; by August 77 data centers and 13 crypto mining sites had answered.
The requests came from a McLennan County resident and four journalists, including a Texas Tribune reporter.
The lawsuit is not a final ruling on release.
quote_evidence: The Public Utility Commission of Texas is asking a Travis County judge to block the release of information showing where data centers and virtual currency mines operate, saying those details could aid terrorists.
The lawsuit does not represent a final ruling on whether the information ultimately must be released.
The commission is not asking the court to declare the entire survey confidential.
why_it_matters_hint: A Texas regulator is fighting disclosure of where data centers sit and how much water and power they use.
notes: The Tribune says one of its reporters is among the people who requested the records; our summary is neutral on that.
